cases.answer: The two sources report slightly different numbers for the same 12-month primary endpoint (freedom from documented AF after a single ablation, mITT population). The primary TAILORED-AF trial (Deisenhofer et al., Nature Medicine 2025) reports the primary efficacy endpoint was achieved in 88% of the tailored arm versus 70% of the anatomical (PVI-only) arm (HR 0.3; 95% CI 0.21–0.57; log-rank P < 0.0001), stated identically in the abstract and the results. The AI-in-AF-management review cites the same trial as showing 12-month freedom from AF of 89% vs. 67% (P < .001), repeating 89% vs. 67% in its evidence table. The difference should be represented as a minor discrepancy/rounding inaccuracy in the review's secondary citation: the trial's authoritative primary values are 88% vs. 70% (an 18-percentage-point absolute difference, P < 0.0001), and the review's 89% vs. 67% (a 22-point gap) slightly overstates the between-arm difference; the primary trial report should be preferred.

cases.ambiguity: The question could be read as asking whether the review's numbers are correct; under that reading the review's 89%/67% slightly misstates the trial's 88%/70% (mITT), and the difference is best represented as an approximate secondary citation with the trial's values taking precedence.
